subject: general
question: Train to Pakistan, a novel set during the Partition of India, was authored by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Khushwant Singh**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Train to Pakistan** is a historical novel by **Khushwant Singh**, published in **1956**. It is widely considered one of the most poignant and realistic literary accounts of the **Partition of India** in **1947**.

• The novel is set in the fictional village of **Mano Majra**, located on the border between **India** and **Pakistan**. It depicts how a peaceful community of **Sikhs** and **Muslims** is torn apart by the external forces of communal hatred and political upheaval.

• The story revolves around the arrival of a **ghost train** carrying the bodies of **Hindu** and **Sikh** refugees from **Pakistan**, which triggers a cycle of revenge and violence in the previously harmonious village.

• The central characters include **Juggut Singh**, a local dacoit who ultimately sacrifices himself to save a train carrying **Muslim** refugees to **Pakistan**, and **Iqbal Singh**, an educated social reformer who finds himself helpless against the rising tide of communal frenzy.

• The book is acclaimed for its **humanistic perspective**, as it avoids taking political sides and instead focuses on the shared suffering, moral dilemmas, and the loss of humanity during the **Partition**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Khushwant Singh (1915–2014):** He was a prominent **Indian author**, **lawyer**, and **journalist**. He served as the editor of **The Illustrated Weekly of India** and was a member of the **Rajya Sabha**. He was awarded the **Padma Bhushan** in **1974** and the **Padma Vibhushan** in **2007**.

• **Vikram Seth:** A celebrated Indian novelist and poet, he is best known for his epic novel **A Suitable Boy**, published in **1993**. His other works include **The Golden Gate** (**1986**) and **An Equal Music** (**1999**).

• **Amrita Pritam:** A legendary **Punjabi** writer and poet, she authored the famous novel **Pinjar** (**1950**), which also deals with the **Partition** and the abduction of women. She was the first woman to win the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1956**.

• **Anita Desai:** A renowned Indian novelist who has been shortlisted for the **Booker Prize** three times. Her works include **Clear Light of Day** (**1980**), which explores the impact of **Partition** on a family in **Old Delhi**, and **In Custody** (**1984**).

• The **Partition of India** in **August 1947** led to the creation of two independent nations, **India** and **Pakistan**, resulting in the displacement of over **14 million** people and widespread communal violence.

**Important Points__**

• The novel **Train to Pakistan** was originally titled **Mano Majra**. It was later adapted into a **film** of the same name in **1998**, directed by **Pamela Rooks**.

• The book highlights the **Radcliffe Line**, the boundary demarcation line that divided the **Punjab** and **Bengal** provinces, which remains a significant geopolitical feature in **South Asia**.

• **Khushwant Singh’s** other notable works include **I Shall Not Hear the Nightingale** (**1959**), **Delhi: A Novel** (**1990**), and his autobiography titled **Truth, Love and a Little Malice** (**2002**).

• The novel is often taught in **literature** and **history** courses globally to provide a **grassroots view** of the social and psychological impact of the **1947** division.

4f
